heard: One Soviet officer prevented a nuclear war by ignoring a missile warning. On September 26, 1983, Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov sat at his console in a secret bunker near Moscow. The early warning computer system reported four additional incoming missiles shortly after the first. Soviet military protocol demanded an immediate counterattack upon receiving such a warning. Petrov reasoned that a real U.S. first strike would involve a massive onslaught of hundreds of missiles, rather than just five. Subsequent investigation determined the false alarm was caused by sunlight reflecting off high-altitude clouds. By treating the warning as a malfunction, instead of reporting an attack, one Soviet officer prevented a nuclear war.
